snippet.title: Why the U.S. Hates Iran?
snippet.description:
Iran's animosity towards the USA is deeply rooted in historical grievances, notably the controversial 1953 coup that ousted Prime Minister Mossadegh and installed the Shah, widely seen as a U.S.-backed intervention. The 1979 Islamic Revolution, which overthrew the Shah, further strained relations, leading to the hostage crisis. Perceived American interference in Iran's domestic affairs, coupled with accusations of supporting opposition groups and imposing economic sanctions, has fueled a persistent distrust. Geopolitical differences, especially regarding regional conflicts and nuclear policies, continue to contribute to the complex and contentious nature of their relationship. The result is a multifaceted dynamic marked by decades of diplomatic challenges and mutual suspicion.
----------------------------------

snippet.title: History Of Kohinoor Diamond
snippet.description:
Checkout Odoo accounting app to manage your entire business easily: https://www.odoo.com/r/1Ko

The Kohinoor’s journey began in India, where it was mined from the legendary Kollur Mine in the Golconda region of present-day Andhra Pradesh. Once considered the largest known diamond in the world, it symbolized immense power. Over centuries, it passed through many rulers — Kakatiyas, Mughals, Persians, Afghans, and Sikhs. In 1849, after the British annexation of Punjab through the Treaty of Lahore, it was taken to London and added to the Crown Jewels under Queen Victoria. Today, housed in the Tower of London, it remains at the centre of global controversy as India, Pakistan, Iran, and Afghanistan demand its return.

Article 370 of the Indian Constitution, originally included as a temporary provision, grants special autonomous status to the region of Jammu and Kashmir. Enacted in 1949, it allows the state to have its own constitution, flag, and governing authority, with the central government's jurisdiction limited to defense, foreign affairs, and communications. Over time, Article 370 has been a subject of controversy, with debates over its effectiveness in maintaining stability in the region versus accusations of perpetuating separatism. Its abrogation in August 2019 by the Indian government sparked both celebration and protest, significantly altering the political landscape of Jammu and Kashmir.

snippet.title: Reality of India's R&AW
snippet.description:
Are you overwhelmed by a plethora of invoices, and have you been losing business due to errors and mistakes in them? It's time to leave conventional methods behind and embrace the digital era with Odoo ERP. Odoo's invoicing app offers swift and efficient invoicing services, managing invoices in a matter of seconds. But that's not all – Odoo provides a suite of other apps for accounting, marketing, sales, HR activities, and more. Make your business operations easy and seamless with Odoo. I tried Odoo's Invoicing app and found it super useful! Exploring the same in this video. Click the link to get started! 
https://www.odoo.com/r/QVM

---------------------------------
The Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) is India's premier intelligence agency, responsible for foreign intelligence gathering, counter-terrorism, and covert operations. Established in 1968, RAW plays a crucial role in ensuring national security and protecting India's interests abroad. Operating under the Cabinet Secretariat, the agency conducts espionage activities, monitors political and military developments in neighboring countries, and combats threats to India’s sovereignty. With its headquarters in New Delhi, RAW has grown into a formidable force, respected and feared globally for its sophisticated intelligence and operational capabilities. Discover more about RAW's intriguing history, missions, and its impact on global intelligence dynamics in this comprehensive overview.

Chara Ghotala refers to the infamous fodder scam in India, a massive corruption scandal involving the embezzlement of public funds earmarked for cattle fodder and livestock development in the Indian state of Bihar (and later Jharkhand). The scam, which surfaced in the 1990s, involved fraudulent withdrawals of over ₹940 crores from the state treasury, facilitated through forged documents, fake bills, and corrupt officials. Prominent political figures, including Lalu Prasad Yadav, were implicated and convicted, making it a landmark case in India's history of political corruption. The scandal highlighted systemic inefficiencies and corruption in government machinery.

snippet.description:

-----------------------------------------------------
Saddam Hussein was a name that evoked fear, power, and controversy across the Middle East. From a poor village near Tikrit to the presidency of Iraq, his journey was marked by war, repression, and ruthless ambition.

He led Iraq through rapid modernization, but it came at the cost of mass killings, the Iran-Iraq War, and the invasion of Kuwait.

After the 2003 US invasion, Saddam disappeared from public view. He was finally captured by American forces in December 2003, found hiding in a small underground bunker near Tikrit.

This video tells the full story from his rise to power to his eventual fall and capture

This video delves into the historical roots of Waqf in India and how its original purpose of charity has been overshadowed by fraud and misuse. Shocking sting operations reveal how caretakers and officials sell or lease these lands at throwaway prices for personal gain. Adding to the controversy is the 2024 Waqf Amendment Bill, which shifts control of Waqf properties to the government, sparking outrage over the loss of community autonomy.

This Waqf story is not just about land or laws but about the lost opportunities for uplifting marginalized communities. If you’ve ever wondered why such vast resources fail to make a difference, this video will leave you with answers—and even more questions. Watch now to understand the scale of the scandal and what it means for India's future.

What began in a small village soon turned into a nationwide Naxal armed movement. In 1967, a peasant uprising in Naxalbari, West Bengal, led by Charu Mazumdar and Kanu Sanyal marked the birth of Naxalism and the rise of CPI (Marxist–Leninist).

Since then, leaders like Kondapalli Seetharamaiah, Ganapathy, and Basavaraj have led powerful groups like CPI (Maoist), expanding the movement deep into India’s tribal and forest regions.

Fueled by land disputes, exploitation, and social inequality, Naxalism has become India’s longest-running internal conflict.

This video covers it all: the origin, the rise, the spread, and how the Indian state has tried to bring it under control.

What began in a small village soon turned into a nationwide Naxal armed movement. In 1967, a peasant uprising in Naxalbari, West Bengal, led by Charu Mazumdar and Kanu Sanyal marked the birth of Naxalism and the rise of CPI (Marxist–Leninist).

Since then, leaders like Kondapalli Seetharamaiah, Ganapathy, and Basavaraj have led powerful groups like CPI (Maoist), expanding the movement deep into India’s tribal and forest regions.

Fueled by land disputes, exploitation, and social inequality, Naxalism has become India’s longest-running internal conflict.

This video covers it all: the origin, the rise, the spread, and how the Indian state has tried to bring it under control.

The 1972 Andes Plane Crash was a harrowing disaster involving a Uruguayan Air Force Fairchild FH-227D aircraft that crashed into the Andes Mountains on October 13, 1972. The flight, carrying 45 passengers and crew, was en route from Montevideo to Santiago when it  encountered severe weather and navigational errors, leading to a crash in a remote and treacherous area. The survivors, facing extreme cold, high altitudes, and dwindling supplies, endured harrowing conditions, resorting to cannibalism to stay alive. After 72 days of struggle, a daring rescue mission led to the survival of 16 individuals, whose ordeal remains a testament to human endurance and resilience.

snippet.title: Kolkata Doctor Case
snippet.description:
Time and again we are reminded of how unsafe is our country for a Women, another crime against a medical student has been reported in Kolkata. This crime occurred within the confines of a medical institution, a place that also serves as the workplace for hundreds of doctors and hospital staff and where thousands come to get treatments.
This crime is not only a despicable act by a criminal but also a glaring failure of the entire system. While there have been some findings related to this incident, the question remains—who is truly to blame? What allowed such an event to transpire within the campus of a medical institution? 
Let's delve into these questions and discuss who is responsible.
----------------------------------
References:
High Court Writ Petition:

The Bangladesh Crisis of 1971, also known as the Bangladesh Liberation War, was a devastating conflict that emerged from rising tensions between East and West Pakistan. Discriminatory policies, economic exploitation, and cultural repression against the Bengali-speaking population in East Pakistan led to mass discontent. This escalated when the West Pakistani military launched a brutal crackdown on March 25, 1971, resulting in widespread atrocities, including massacres and targeted violence against civilians. The crisis triggered a mass exodus of refugees into neighboring India and culminated in a war between India and Pakistan. After months of intense fighting, Bangladesh emerged as an independent nation on December 16, 1971, marking the end of one of the bloodiest conflicts in South Asian history.

snippet.title: Why Dollar Is A Global Currency?
snippet.description:
Get the right skills to excel in the field of Data Science and Machine Learning. Check out: 

https://www.scaler.com/?utm_source=brandedcontent&utm_medium=NitishRajputDecember2023&utm_campaign=brand_scaler_academy_brandedcontent_NitishRajputDec2023_branded-content-video-campaign-NitishRajputDec2023-18Dec2023_india_all&utm_id=brandedcontent&utm_content=YT-description

#SCALER #WhereTheHungryLearn
----------------------------------
The US Dollar's status as the primary international currency stems from a combination of historical strength after World War II, the Bretton Woods Agreement, and the United States' pivotal role in global trade and finance.
